question: A basic solution will have a pH:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Greater than 7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pH scale** is a tool used to measure how **acidic** or **basic** (alkaline) a water-based solution is. The scale typically ranges from **0 to 14**.
 
• A **basic solution** is defined as having a **pH value greater than 7**. This indicates a higher concentration of **hydroxide ions (OH-)** relative to **hydrogen ions (H+)**. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***
 
• At a standard temperature of **25°C (298 K)**, a solution with a **pH equal to 7** is considered **neutral**, meaning the concentrations of **H+** and **OH-** ions are perfectly balanced. Pure water is a classic example of a neutral substance.
 
• Solutions with a **pH less than 7** are classified as **acidic**. The lower the **pH value**, the stronger the **acidity** of the solution, representing a high concentration of **hydrogen ions**.
 
• The term **pH** stands for **"potential of Hydrogen"** or **"power of Hydrogen"**. It is mathematically calculated as the **negative logarithm** (base 10) of the **molar concentration** of hydrogen ions in the solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Bases:**
 
 
• **Bases** have a **bitter taste** and a **slippery or soapy feel** to the touch.
 
• In chemical testing, **bases** turn **red litmus paper** to **blue** and turn **phenolphthalein** indicator **pink**.
 
• Common examples of **basic substances** include **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, also known as caustic soda, **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)**, and **Ammonia (NH3)**.
 
• Daily life examples of **bases** include **baking soda**, **antacids**, **soap**, and **bleach**.
 
 
 
• **Strong vs. Weak Bases:**
 
 
• A **strong base** is one that **fully dissociates** into its ions in an aqueous solution, such as **Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• A **weak base** only **partially dissociates** in water, such as **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)**.
 
 
 
• **pH and pOH Relationship:**
 
 
• In any aqueous solution at **25°C**, the sum of **pH** and **pOH** (potential of hydroxide) always equals **14**.
 
• This relationship is derived from the **ionic product of water (Kw)**, which is **1.0 x 10^-14** at room temperature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Logarithmic Nature:** The **pH scale** is **logarithmic**, meaning each whole **pH value** below **7** is **ten times** more acidic than the next higher value. For instance, a solution with **pH 4** is **10 times** more acidic than **pH 5** and **100 times** more acidic than **pH 6**.
 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** The **neutral point** of the **pH scale** is exactly **7** only at **25°C**. If the **temperature** increases, the **auto-ionization** of water increases, which can lower the **pH value** of neutral water even though it remains chemically neutral.
 
• **Measurement Tools:** **pH** can be measured using **universal indicators**, **pH paper**, or high-precision electronic devices called **pH meters**, which measure the **electromotive force** between electrodes placed in the solution.
 
• **Biological Significance:** Most biological fluids in the **human body**, such as **blood**, are slightly **basic**, with a **pH** maintained strictly between **7.35 and 7.45**.
